successors.name: Principality of Wales
successors.text: Harlech surrendered in February 1409; Owain disappeared after 1412

ledger.x: 1400: Owain Glyndwr is proclaimed Prince of Wales.
1404: mirrors marcher-lordships' contest over the south-east March; which lordships Owain held is not on the pages (confidence 1).
1404: mirrors marcher-lordships' contest over Glamorgan and Pembrokeshire ('continued to ravage the south by burning Cardiff Castle', 1404).
1404: mirrors marcher-lordships' contest over Powys, Brecknock and Denbighshire; Owain's own country (Sycharth, 1400).
May 1405: the south-east is lost after the defeats of early 1405 and Pwll Melyn ('in May 1405'); the Glyndwr Rising page dates Grosmont and Usk to 1406 (the pages disagree by a year).
1406 (late): 'the resistance in Anglesey formally ended toward the end of 1406'.
By 1407: 'the English had recaptured Anglesey and large parts of south Wales'; 'One by one the Lordships began to surrender'.
1407: 'the superior numbers, resources, and wealth that England had at its disposal began to turn the tide of the war'; by 1409 only Harlech and Aberystwyth were left (bridge, confidence 1).
By 1407: 'large parts of south Wales' recaptured (Glyndwr Rising page); Carmarthenshire is the researcher's reading.
1409 (February): Harlech falls and the rising loses its last castle.

wars.name: Glyndŵr Rising
wars.outcome: Most of Wales held 1404-1408; Aberystwyth and Harlech lost 1408-1409; pardons offered by Henry V in 1415 and 1416; Owain presumed dead about 1416.

certainty.note: Castle sieges, not borders; 'most of Wales' is the page's only extent.
